track: Track B adjacent fair-exit instrument architecture
journal_volume_issue_year: FEC Systems & Structures, draft dated March 20, 2016
author: The Mothership LLC; shared by the Federation of Egalitarian Communities
page_locator: Voluntary Withdrawal; Sections 10.1-10.2; Leaving Fund; Retirement Fund; Dispute Resolution
source_access: complete public HTML transcription of an explicitly labelled draft agreement inspected
evidence_type: primary draft operating instrument; execution and implementation not verified
exact_factual_observation: The draft permits a member to withdraw for any or no reason on 30 days' written notice. It requires a Leaving Fund for every member, payment within two business days after withdrawal or expulsion, enough cash on hand to pay all such funds, monthly contributions for the first 40 months, and CPI adjustment. A separate Retirement Fund begins later, is expressly nonvested, need not be held in cash, and may be paid as a ten-year annuity or as a six-month lump sum worth half its stated value. Members receive record access and internally prepared financial statements. Agreement disputes move from negotiation to mutually acceptable mediation and then arbitration, with parties initially paying their own expenses and sharing neutral costs.
what_source_establishes: A written exit instrument can separate the permission to leave, notice, immediate liquidity, reserve sufficiency, later benefits, records, debt priority, and dispute forum. The two-business-day Leaving Fund and all-member cash reserve make the immediate payment independently testable before a crisis. The same text also shows that a prompt small fund can coexist with a slower, nonvested, or discounted larger benefit.
what_source_does_not_establish: The document is explicitly a draft with sample names and blank signatures. It does not establish adoption, capitalization, compliance, any actual exit or payout, the sufficiency of either fund for relocation, independent valuation or escrow, former-member record access, a safety exception to notice, housing or medical continuity, family contact, dependent support, or a later member outcome. Arbitration cost-sharing may be unusable for a cash-poor leaver, and community payment of those costs remains subject to member consensus.
author_interpretation: The instrument treats withdrawal as available without cause, ring-fences a short-term leaving fund, indexes it, keeps accounting records, orders debt and member distributions on dissolution, and supplies a staged dispute route.
alternative_interpretation: Thirty days' notice can protect operational continuity, a retirement haircut can protect collective solvency, and internal consensus can reduce administrative cost. Those purposes do not establish that the amounts, timing, or review are usable for a particular household, and the draft may have functioned only as a teaching template.
response_process: written withdrawal notice or expulsion; membership ends; Leaving Fund due within two business days; former member requests or otherwise triggers Retirement Fund disbursement; negotiation, mediation, arbitration, and enforceable judgment for disputes. No emergency housing, family-contact, or safety sequence is specified.
outcome: No executed agreement, reserve statement, payout, dispute result, relocation, family continuity, or later wellbeing outcome was located. This is an architecture finding, not an effectiveness finding.
transferability: High for drafting a distinct immediate exit reserve, a fixed deadline, CPI adjustment, record access, debt priority, and an external dispute endpoint. Equally high for testing benefit vesting, payout haircut, former-member access, household sufficiency, safety exceptions, neutral valuation, escrow, and cost barriers. Low for treating this draft or any specific dollar amount as a validated model.
likely_article_destination: Fair separation / money and land / children's outward door
notes: The source page labels the agreement DRAFT 03/20/2016 and shows placeholder signatories. Preserve that status in every use. Do not infer execution or recommend a 30-day delay where immediate lawful safety action is required. Moora Moora's public manifesto was inspected only as a comparator because it says its figures are not current and points to nonpublic formal rules.

journal_volume_issue_year: FEC public project page; 2013 administrator interview
author: Federation of Egalitarian Communities; Laird Schaub interviewed by Mira Luna
community_group: Preservation of Equity Accessible for Community Health (PEACH)
page_locator: FEC PEACH page; GEO account paragraphs on contributions, claims, governance, and reported outcomes
source_access: current official organization page and 2013 first-person administrator interview inspected; no governing rules, claim ledger, audit, or legal-status record located
evidence_type: organization-level primary governance statement plus first-person historical claim account
exact_factual_observation: The current FEC page says PEACH is governed separately from FEC delegates by one representative of each participating community and administered by a technical officer. The 2013 interview account says communities, not individuals, participate: a community decides and files a member-related claim after paying the cost. It describes reimbursement of 90 percent above a $5,000 community threshold up to a formula-based annual limit, and a 90 percent contribution refund to a community that leaves, net of reimbursements. It also reports approximately one claim a year among about 200 people in eight communities and says all but one claim had been paid, while expressly stating that the agreement gave no direct right to an individual.
what_source_establishes: A federation can separate its general delegates from a pooled-risk governing body, specify contributions, attachment, reimbursement, annual exposure, investment, and organizational withdrawal, and preserve equity between participating institutions. The record also establishes a structural member-rights gap: the individual depends on the home community to approve, finance, and transmit the claim before the federation-level process begins.
what_source_does_not_establish: The records do not supply the actual rules, current contribution or reserve, legal classification, audit, claim or denial ledger, coverage definitions, medical-necessity standard, individual notice or appeal, hardship bridge, conflict rule, demographic denominator, later claim history, or claimant outcomes. The current official page corroborates governance but not the 2013 payment assertion. Paying nearly every filed claim would not show how many needs were never filed by a community.
author_interpretation: Schaub presented trust between individuals, communities, and the pooled body as central and treated the income-sharing population as unusually selected; the account identifies changing age mix and medical costs as future risks.
alternative_interpretation: Community-level responsibility and a small trusted pool may permit low administration and flexible coverage. The same structure can hide an individual's denied or delayed need before it becomes a PEACH claim, while the reported low claim rate may reflect health, age, narrow submission, exclusions, or incomplete reporting rather than fund performance alone.
response_process: individual medical need; home-community decision and upfront payment; community claim; formula-limited PEACH reimbursement; representative-body governance. No individual external intake, denial notice, hardship bridge, appeal, independent medical review, or later outcome sequence is documented.
outcome: The 2013 account reported a large reserve, roughly one claim per year, and all claims paid except one. No audited denominator, current balance, current claim disposition, individual care outcome, or legal-operational status was located in the inspected current page.
transferability: High for mapping the two gatekeeper layers and requiring individual notice, direct independent appeal, emergency care, audited filed and unfiled needs, denial and delay records, portability, legal review, and later patient outcomes. Medium for organization-level reserve design. Zero for transferring medical decision authority to a private community or treating the historical record as current coverage.
likely_article_destination: Medicine / money and land / external couplings / outcome dashboard
notes: The source uses self-insurance language; this ledger does not independently classify PEACH under insurance law. Preserve patient choice and licensed independent medical judgment. Do not convert age, illness, cost, disability, or community membership into a danger or admission screen.

track: Track B adjacent planned-fission and allocation boundary
journal_volume_issue_year: Walter Estate v. Walter, 1986; current Hutterites.org public record
article_title: Court allocation after colony dissolution and customary daughter-colony formation
author: Alberta Court of Appeal; Hutterites.org member editors
community_group: Felger Hutterite Colony; Hutterite daughter-colony practice
page_locator: Walter Estate appeal and Hutterites.org Daughter Colony sections
source_access: reported appellate judgment and official member-managed public account inspected; underlying trust agreement, trial judgment, and specific planned-division schedule not obtained
evidence_type: primary legal allocation record kept distinct from a primary community public account of planned fission
exact_factual_observation: In Walter Estate v. Walter, the Alberta Court of Appeal affirmed a trial allocation after the Felger Colony partnership dissolved: nine partners shared according to length of service, with the deceased comptroller's estate reduced for funds the courts found had been diverted to a breakaway colony. That was a dissolution allocation, not a planned daughter split. Separately, Hutterites.org says colonies near 30 families or 150 people prepare a daughter site and value and divide aggregate assets; people may volunteer to move or be divided into groups and assigned by lot. In the described Lehrerleut process, every family packs before the lot and the selected group may leave in one day.
what_source_establishes: A primary allocation judgment can resolve beneficiary shares after institutional breakdown, while a planned-fission record can specify a scale trigger, capital runway, aggregate asset valuation, and successor formation before crisis. Placing the records side by side shows that aggregate parity, judicial allocation, and individual choice are separate questions: an asset-balanced split can still assign a household by lot, and a later court allocation is not a preexisting voluntary fork protocol.
what_source_does_not_establish: The appellate record does not reproduce the 1972 trust agreement, the unreported trial judgment, every asset value, actual payment timing, independent advice, or later partner and breakaway-colony outcomes. The daughter-colony page gives no named case, signed agreement, debt and valuation schedule, individual refusal or appeal right, child or spouse voice, parity audit, or comparative successor outcome. It does not establish that every Hutterite colony follows the same practice.
author_interpretation: The public Hutterite account presents daughter formation as an expected response to scale and work constraints, recognizes variation among branches, and openly notes that selection and moving can be painful.
alternative_interpretation: Volunteering and lot-casting may be understood internally as legitimate, impartial, or religiously meaningful, and service-length allocation may reflect contribution and anti-unjust-enrichment concerns. Those interpretations do not make either mechanism a transferable consent process or prove equal consequences for every person.
response_process: dissolution dispute; court identification and allocation among beneficiaries; appellate affirmance. Separately: scale threshold; land purchase and construction; aggregate asset valuation; volunteer formation or group division; lot; rapid relocation; separate colony operation. No common individual refusal, neutral appeal, or later-outcome process appears across the records.
outcome: Walter reports a legal allocation endpoint but no human or successor outcome. Hutterites.org reports formation mechanics and pain but no comparative debt, viability, family-contact, member-choice, or later wellbeing result. A 2021 field study adds that some successor colonies face long financial strain, but the cited primary allocation itself was not directly accessible.
transferability: High for separating planned fission from conflict dissolution and for requiring individual opt-in or refusal, household and child voice, transparent asset and debt schedules, independent advice, appeal, both-successor liquidity, family contact, and fixed later reviews. Low for importing lot-casting, religious allocation, or judicial dissolution as a modern general recommendation.
likely_article_destination: Forks are the immune system / money and land / outcome dashboard
notes: Keep the Felger dissolution judgment, customary daughter-colony account, and 2021 field study separate. No forced relocation, banishment, family division, or compelled association follows. Retrieve the trust agreement, trial reasons, a signed daughter-colony schedule, dissent records, and both-successor accounts before claiming a complete fission protocol.

track: Track B adjacent court-supervised trust closure
journal_volume_issue_year: High Court order dated July 25, 2025; JFCT status through March 2026
article_title: Schedule 1A – the Notice and current closure phases
author: High Court of Justice; Jesus Fellowship Community Trust trustees
community_group: Jesus Fellowship Community Trust / former New Creation Christian Community
page_locator: Notice pp. 1-4; closure Phases 1-4; March 2026 update
source_access: complete official notice and current official closure pages inspected; complete order and Trust Deed not obtained because the public notice directed readers to request them
evidence_type: judgment-derived claim notice and current trust-deed-based distribution record
exact_factual_observation: The notice required anyone pursuing specified claims outside the Trust Deed and listed-beneficiary position to provide identity, factual and legal basis, supporting evidence, and amount or calculation by October 16, 2025. It says trustees would classify timely claims as rejected or pending resolution, could distribute without regard to covered claims not timely preserved, and would not pay claimants' legal costs. The official phase page separates initial transition distributions, redress and claims, historic requests, and residual apportionment; several later payments depend on defined records, deadlines, and votes of Listed Beneficiaries. The trustees reported the court claims procedure complete on January 23, 2026, and March 2026 deed amendments opened two additional Phase 3 categories whose registration window closed April 30, 2026.
what_source_establishes: A court-supervised closure can separate redress, civil claims, historic requests, transition payments, and residual apportionment, demand a stated factual and legal basis before assets are distributed, and create a recorded endpoint. It also demonstrates why a fair-exit right must exist before collapse: late access may depend on archived institutional records, a short claim window, self-funded legal advice, trustee screening, and a beneficiary vote rather than an automatic portable entitlement.
what_source_does_not_establish: The public materials do not reproduce the full Order or complete Trust Deed, show each claimant's notice and advice access, establish whether trustee classification or beneficiary voting was fair in a particular case, report all distributions, or give later housing, pension, family-contact, survivor, child, or wellbeing outcomes. Court supervision and a completed claims procedure do not establish completed trust closure or fair individual exit.
author_interpretation: The trustees describe the phased sequence as following legal priority, the Trust Deed, beneficiary votes, and High Court direction, and sought the court process so later distributions could proceed without unresolved claim uncertainty.
alternative_interpretation: A firm cut-off and required particulars can preserve a finite fund, prevent double recovery, and give trustees finality; beneficiary votes may implement the deed's associative bargain. Those functions can coexist with cost, record, notice, capacity, or timing barriers for former members and do not substitute for a standing pre-crisis exit mechanism.
response_process: notice of potential claim; identity, evidence, legal basis, and amount; trustee classification; litigation if necessary; claims-procedure completion; later deed-governed votes and distributions. Redress, court claims, historic requests, and residual apportionment remain separate, and no ordinary member-exit process is supplied by the closure record.
outcome: The court claims procedure was declared complete in January 2026 and the additional registration window closed in April 2026. Phase votes, final distributions, expected long-tail administration, final closure, and recipient outcomes were not complete in the inspected record.
transferability: High for predefining claim categories, record custody, notice, advice support, independent classification and appeal, deadlines with accessibility safeguards, debt and claim priority, double-recovery rules, and published distribution outcomes. Low for treating this exceptional closure as an ordinary exit template, and zero for privately extinguishing legal rights without applicable law, due process, and independent advice.
likely_article_destination: Fair separation / money and land / external legal couplings / outcome dashboard
notes: This is a current procedural record as of August 15, 2026, not a prediction of later votes or payments. Do not combine redress eligibility, civil liability, historic-request voting, and residual beneficiary status. A procedural deadline is not evidence of recovery, family repair, or material exit usability.
